sections.h2: What should an Iowa home seller know about the state?
sections.html:
Iowa is a landlocked Midwest state of 56,273 square miles, with the Mississippi River on the east and the Missouri and Big Sioux Rivers on the west. It had 3,190,369 residents at the 2020 census, according to Wikipedia's Iowa entry, and the state is divided into 99 counties.

Property rules in Iowa are set at the state level and applied by each county. That means a seller in a small county and a seller in the capital follow the same statutes, though the offices, forms and local levies differ.

This page gives the statewide picture. The city and county guides listed above go deeper on a single place.

sections.h2: Which Iowa cities and counties are the largest?
sections.html:
Des Moines is the largest city and the state capital. The 2020 census counts for the five biggest cities are shown below.

City2020 populationCounty
Des Moines214,133Polk
Cedar Rapids137,710Linn
Davenport101,724Scott
Sioux City85,797Woodbury
Iowa City74,828Johnson

Other populous counties include Black Hawk, whose seat is Waterloo, plus Dallas, Story, Dubuque and Pottawattamie. Council Bluffs sits in the Omaha metro area, which reaches across the river into Iowa.

County seats do not always match the biggest city. Dallas County's seat is Adel and Story County's is Nevada. Lee County has two seats, Fort Madison and Keokuk, which is why Iowa has 100 county seats for 99 counties.

sections.h2: How is Iowa divided into regions?
sections.html:
The land changes noticeably from west to east, and it affects the kind of house you find. The Loess Hills run along the western border, where wind-blown deposits are several hundred feet thick in places. Northeast Iowa is the Driftless Area, with steep hills and deep valleys.

The rest of the state is mostly farmland in the center and north, where corn, soybeans and hogs dominate. A house in a Driftless valley town and one on a central Iowa farm tract sit in very different settings, which is one reason the local guides matter.

sections.h2: What does the Iowa economy mean for a house sale?
sections.html:
Manufacturing is the largest sector, with food processing, heavy machinery and agricultural chemicals leading. Finance and insurance, information technology, biotechnology, government and wind power round out the list.

Companies with large Iowa operations include John Deere, Principal Financial, Pella Corporation, Vermeer and Hy-Vee. Agriculture stays important to the state, though it makes up a smaller share of the overall economy than many people expect.

For a seller, local employers shape who can buy. The farm crisis of the 1980s caused a major recession and population loss in Iowa, a reminder of how closely housing follows jobs here.

sections.h2: How do roads, rail and airports connect Iowa places?
sections.html:
Four interstates carry most traffic. I-80 runs east to west through Council Bluffs, Des Moines and Iowa City. I-35 crosses the middle of the state through Des Moines, and I-29 follows the western edge through Council Bluffs and Sioux City. I-74 begins at I-80 near Davenport, and I-380 runs from near Iowa City through Cedar Rapids to Waterloo.

  • Airports: Des Moines International, Eastern Iowa Airport in Cedar Rapids, and Quad City International in Moline, Illinois, with smaller fields at Dubuque and Waterloo.
  • Rail: Amtrak's California Zephyr stops in Burlington, Ottumwa and Creston, and the Southwest Chief serves Fort Madison.
  • Transit: Cyride, Cedar Rapids Transit and Des Moines Area Regional Transit.

sections.h2: What weather risks affect Iowa houses?
sections.html:
Iowa has a humid continental climate with real extremes. Summer highs can approach 90 degrees Fahrenheit and occasionally pass 100, and winter lows can fall below minus 18.

Severe weather season starts in spring. The 30-year average is about 47 tornadoes a year, and twelve people died in tornadoes in 2008. Roofs, siding and windows therefore carry weight in inspections, and so do basements in river towns.

Sellers with storm damage, an old roof or an unfinished repair can sell as is to a cash buyer rather than fix the house first. The county assessor and your insurer can tell you how a past claim or a disaster declaration affects your situation, including the protest window for assessments, which moves to May 1 through June 5 in a declared disaster county.

sections.h2: How does Iowa property tax work across counties?
sections.html:
Counties bill in two installments, and the first becomes delinquent on October 1 and the second on April 1 under Iowa Code 445.37. When the last day of September or March falls on a weekend, delinquency moves to the second business day of the next month.

Assessments are generally updated every two years. Owners can protest with the local board of review from April 2 through April 30 of the assessment year, on grounds such as an unequal assessment, a value above what the law allows, a misclassification or an error. Starting January 1, 2027, the burden of proof shifts to the assessor when an assessment rises more than 10 percent, according to the Iowa League of Cities.

For fiscal year 2027, the residential rollback is 44.5345 percent. Homes with three or more units move to a separate multi-residential class on January 1, 2027, while duplexes and single-family homes remain residential.

sections.h2: What changed in the Iowa homestead benefit?
sections.html:
The homestead tax credit became a homestead exemption of 10 percent of taxable value, with a $5,500 minimum and a $20,000 maximum, under SF 2472 signed May 18, 2026. It applies from assessment year 2026, so the first effect appears on taxes paid in September 2027.

Owners 65 and older qualify for an extra $6,500 of taxable value. Owners who had the credit before July 1, 2026 are moved over automatically. The details are in our statewide homestead guide and on the Department of Revenue page.

The exemption ends when the house is sold, so a buyer files a new application with the county assessor.

sections.h2: What are the state rules for recording and transferring a house?
sections.html:
Iowa charges a real estate transfer tax of eighty cents for each $500 of value above the first $500, under Iowa Code 428A.1. It is paid to the recorder of the county where the property sits, and the amount must appear on the face of the document.

A declaration of value, signed by at least one seller or buyer or an agent, goes in with each recorded deed. The recorder forwards it to the assessor. A transfer with no consideration is not taxed.

  • The price of any personal property sold with the house can be subtracted if stated on the instrument.
  • Assumed liens count as part of the price.
  • Corrective title documents that say so are exempt.

New 2026 laws also require homeowners associations to certify whether dues are current and to disclose approved upcoming assessments and transfer fees. Counties must now allow at least one accessory dwelling unit on a lot with a single-family home wherever such homes are allowed.

sections.h2: How do state topics change the way an Iowa house sells?
sections.html:
Each situation has its own timeline, and Iowa law sets most of them. A tenant dispute follows the three-day, seven-day and 30-day notices in Iowa Code chapter 562A. A death in the family can bring a probate process and, for deaths before 2025, a possible inheritance tax file, since the tax no longer applies to deaths on or after January 1, 2025.

Unpaid property tax runs on the delinquency dates above, and other problems such as a quitclaim deed, a sheriff sale or a capital gains question each have their own guide on this site.

If you are not sure which of these applies to your house, tell us the address and the situation. We buy Iowa houses as they stand and can explain how each path would work for you.

faqs.q: How many counties does Iowa have?
faqs.a: Iowa has 99 counties. It has 100 county seats because Lee County has two, Fort Madison and Keokuk.

faqs.q: When are Iowa property taxes due?
faqs.a: The first installment is delinquent from October 1 and the second from April 1. If the last day of September or March is a weekend, delinquency starts on the second business day of the next month.

faqs.q: What is the Iowa real estate transfer tax?
faqs.a: It is eighty cents for each $500 of value above the first $500, paid to the county recorder with a declaration of value. Transfers with no consideration are not taxed.

faqs.q: Can I protest my Iowa assessment?
faqs.a: Yes. File with your local board of review between April 2 and April 30, or May 1 to June 5 if your county is under a disaster declaration. A written protest on the state form is required.

faqs.q: What is the Iowa homestead exemption worth?
faqs.a: It is 10 percent of taxable value, between $5,500 and $20,000 for assessment year 2026, plus an extra $6,500 for owners 65 and older.

faqs.q: Does Iowa still have an inheritance tax?
faqs.a: No. The Department of Revenue states the tax does not apply to deaths on or after January 1, 2025.
